items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So I was really, really upset when I couldn’t play with the band, when he called and told me and said, “I’m sorry, baby, but you got to go.”

ctx.x: Did she wind up singing with the band?

You bet. I never saw the huge crowds I used to see with us. But they made their money and he was happy, and I think that’s so beautiful. He ended up having quite a career himself. He changed his name. He took his real name. He was a cousin of John Lee Hooker. His name was Floyd Lee. It was probably some of the happiest moments of my life. I remember playing in the summer, and having heat exhaustion. I remember he would put a bag of ice under his bowler hat in the summer when it was so hot. And I remember playing…
Let’s step back for a minute.
